words.gloss: so as to enter the mind

literal: Among the learned, the learned they will be called, who before the learned, what they learned, so as to enter their minds, speak.
translation: Those who can speak what they have learned in such a way that it deeply enters the minds of the learned assembled before them, will be regarded as the most learned among the learned.
modern: கற்றறிந்த அறிஞர்களின் முன்னிலையில், தாம் கற்றவற்றை அவர்களின் மனதில் பதியும்படி எடுத்துச் சொல்ல வல்லவர்கள், கற்றவர்களுக்கெல்லாம் கற்றவர் என்று போற்றப்படுவர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that true scholarship is validated only when it can be communicated effectively to other scholars. The word 'செல' literally means 'to go' or 'to enter', which in this context means making one's ideas penetrate and be accepted by the minds of the audience. It is not enough to merely possess knowledge; one must have the courage and skill to articulate it clearly before an assembly of experts. Those who can successfully convey their learning to other learned people are crowned as the best among scholars.
